meanings.note: Серьёзный человек. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ерьёзный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('serious; important, influential').

Серьёзный человек. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ерьёзный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('serious; important, influential').

examples.text: Я приехала к очень серьёзному человеку.
examples.trans: I have come to see a very important man.

examples.text: Я приехала к очень серьёзному человеку. Он меня ждёт.
examples.trans: I have come to see a very important man. He is waiting for me.

meanings.note: Adverb of degree. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ильно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ложный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('complicated, difficult').

examples.trans: Danila, let's go. Look, there's nothing complicated.

meanings.note: Сломать руку = to break one's arm. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ломать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to break', paired with 'ломать'.

examples.text: Меня жена бросила. Два пальца сломаны.
examples.trans: My wife has left me. Two of my fingers are broken.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'body-breaker (jocular)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы же телохранители, а не телоломатели.
Этих грозных охранников в шутку прозвали телоломателями.
examples.trans: Those formidable guards were jokingly nicknamed body-breakers.

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'bodyguard' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Уходи! = Go away!. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away', paired with 'уйти'.

meanings.en: to participate, to take part (в + prepositional)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'частвовать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to participate, to take part'.

examples.trans: I am taking part in the election.

examples.text: Как вы знаете, Виталий, я участвую в выборах.
examples.trans: As you know, Vitaly, I am taking part in the election.

examples.text: Но я в этих махинациях не участвовал!
examples.trans: But I did not participate in these schemes!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'philosopher' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Listen to me carefully, you philosophers!

examples.text: Послушайте меня внимательно, философы! Я вам отдал приказ!
examples.trans: Listen to me carefully, you philosophers! I gave you an order!
What thing did you realize, philosopher?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
